title: The 'Can't Tell Ward', Paoletti's band, and Black bands Laine never heard
summary: Allen explains the Seventh Ward and asks about Paoletti and Vesey bands; Laine does not know them and never attended Black funeral marches.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Well, he should have been from the Seventh Ward. You know what they call the Seventh Ward? The what? They changed the word line so many times. No, no, no. You know what they call it around St. Bernard Avenue? They call that the Can't Tell Ward. Tell him. I don't still get it. Tell him. Along about St. Bernard Avenue, they call that the Can't Tell Ward, because you can't tell if they're white or colored. What about Paoletti's band? Who? Paoletti. Baoletti? Paoletti. Paoletti. Paoletti. Paoletti. Letty? Paoletti. Paoletti. You don't remember that name? No. No. Don't remember. I see. Dick's going to tell you. Paoletti had a band out at West End, you know, and played on the lakefront. And he'd play around Spanish for it a lot. He had a big band.
Well, I played out there all the time. I had bands out there regular. You played at the West End? Well, I never heard of this band.

What about Almond Vesey? Never heard of him. Never heard of him. They may have been after your time, Papa. Must have been late bands. Must have been. Yeah. It couldn't have been around my time. Papa, let me ask you something. Did you ever go to any colored funeral marches when you were a child? No. Never did go to those colored funerals? No. No.
Well, then you don't really know what the colored people were playing when you were growing up. No. I see. No.
